BGY1.claim: Gaya, Bihar's second-largest city, lies 100 km south of Patna on the Phalgu River and is holy to Hindus, Buddhists and Jains; it is ringed by rocky hills on three sides.

evidence.quote: Gaya Ji is the second largest city of Bihar, India, and it is also headquarter of Gaya Ji District.
Gaya Ji is situated 100 km south of Patna, the capital city of Bihar. This ancient city grew on the banks of Phalgu River (Niranjana, as mentioned in Ramayana).

This place is considered holy among the Hindus, the Buddhists and the Jains. It is surrounded by small rocky hills (Mangla-Gauri, Shringa-Sthan, Ram-Shila and Brahmayoni) by three sides and the river flowing on the fourth (eastern) side.
It is surrounded by small rocky hills (Mangla-Gauri, Shringa-Sthan, Ram-Shila and Brahmayoni) by three sides and the river flowing on the fourth (eastern) side.

BGY2.claim: The city takes its name from the mythological demon Gayasur; the Vishnupad Temple is open 5 am to 9 pm, and Mangala Gauri is about 8 km away up a hill.

evidence.quote: Gaya Ji derives its name from the mythological demon Gayasur (which literally means Gaya Ji the demon).
Vishnupad temple How to Reach? Auto-rickshaws and cycle-rickshaws within Gaya Ji. Timings 5 AM to 9 PM
Mangala Gauri How to Reach About 8 km from Gaya Ji.

BGY3.claim: Gaya International Airport serves the area; the train from Patna takes about 2 hours; auto-rickshaws and cycle-rickshaws get around town.

evidence.quote: Nearest Airport Gaya International Airport
It takes approximately 2 hours to reach Gaya Ji from Patna by Train.
Auto-rickshaws and cycle-rickshaws within Gaya Ji.

BGY5.claim: The Phalgu is the Niranjana of the Ramayana; the hills include Mangla-Gauri, Ram-Shila and Brahmayoni; the Vishnupad Temple is a major pind daan site, and Gaya also witnessed the Buddha's enlightenment.

Mangla-Gauri, Shringa-Sthan, Ram-Shila and Brahmayoni

BVP1.claim: The Vishnupad Temple in Gaya, built in 1787 by Queen Ahilyabai, enshrines a footprint of Vishnu in rock and is a major site for pind daan.

evidence.quote: The temple was erected during 1787 by Queen Ahilyabai. A beautiful sacred place on the banks of Phalgu river surrounded by rugged rocks on three sides and water on the fourth side.
It is famous for the sacred footprint of Vishnu, which is enshrined in a rock. The temple is also a major site for performing "Pind Daan," a Hindu ritual for the salvation of ancestors.

The temple is also a major site for performing "Pind Daan," a Hindu ritual for the salvation of ancestors. The temple’s riverside location and architectural grandeur make it an essential spiritual destination.

BVP2.claim: Best September to April; mobiles, cameras and other electronic gadgets are prohibited; dress modestly and remove footwear.

evidence.quote: Best Time to Visit : September to April.
Electronic Gadgets : Mobile, Camera, Electronic Gadgets Prohibited.
Dress modestly, remove footwear before entering

BVP3.claim: The Ramayana tells that Rama came to Gaya to perform pind daan for his father Dasharatha; the temple stands on the Phalgu.

evidence.quote: where Lord Rama went to Gaya Ji to do pind-daan of his father Dashrath
A beautiful sacred place on the banks of Phalgu river

BGB1.claim: The 80-foot Great Buddha in Bodh Gaya, of sandstone blocks and red granite, was consecrated by the 14th Dalai Lama on 18 November 1989; its foundation stone was laid in 1982.

evidence.quote: The great statue is a mix of sandstone blocks and red granite. It is possibly the largest built in India and was consecrated on 18 November 1989 by the 14th Dalai Lama.
was consecrated on 18 November 1989 by the 14th Dalai Lama

The foundation stone for the statue was placed in 1982. Gaya THU 21 °C FRI 21 °C SAT 21 °C SUN 21 °C Photo Gallery At a Glance One of the tallest Buddha statues in India, this magnificent 80-foot-tall structure in Bodh Gaya was inaugurated in 1989.

BGB2.claim: It shows the Buddha in deep meditation, surrounded by smaller statues of his disciples; it is about 2 km from the Mahabodhi Temple and open 24 hours.

evidence.quote: depicts Lord Buddha in deep meditation
The statue is surrounded by smaller statues of Buddha’s disciples
The 80 Feet Buddha is around 2 km away
Timings Open 24 hours

BGB3.claim: One of the tallest Buddha statues in India; reachable by local auto, e-rickshaw or taxi; Gaya International Airport is about 7 km away.

evidence.quote: One of the tallest Buddha statues in India
can be reached easily by local auto, e-rickshaw or taxi
Gaya International Airport is about 7 km away

BGB4.claim: Etiquette: dress modestly and maintain silence.

evidence.quote: Dress modestly; maintain silence

BBS1.claim: Buddha Smriti Park, a 22-acre park on Fraser Road near Patna Junction, was built by the Bihar government for the Buddha's 2554th birth anniversary; two Bodhi trees planted by the Dalai Lama flank its Buddha statue.

evidence.quote: The Buddha Smriti Park was developed by the Government of Bihar to commemorate the 2554th birthday of Lord Buddha. It is an urban oasis sprawling across a generous area of 22 acre.
It is an urban oasis sprawling across a generous area of 22 acre. The highlight of the park are two Bodhi trees, planted by the Dalai Lama, which flank a statue of Lord Buddha.

The highlight of the park are two Bodhi trees, planted by the Dalai Lama, which flank a statue of Lord Buddha. Also known as the Buddha Memorial Park, it is located on Frazer Road near Patna Junction, opposite the Mahavir Mandir.
it is located on Frazer Road near Patna Junction, opposite the Mahavir Mandir

BBS2.claim: The 200-ft Pataliputra Karuna Stupa holds a Buddha relic from Vaishali; the park also has a meditation centre with 60 cells, a library and a museum.

evidence.quote: The 200-ft-high Pataliputra Karuna Stupa is a circular structure that is the most prominent feature of the park. It has several entrances and houses a relic of Lord Buddha, which is one of the eight original relics excavated from Vaishali, in a glass enclosure.
houses a relic of Lord Buddha, which is one of the eight original relics excavated from Vaishali
It has 60 cells and one can view the beautiful stupa from each of them. Along with artefacts, there are audio-visual and multimedia presentations about the life and teachings of Buddha in the museum.

BBS3.claim: Open 9 am to 6 pm; entry ₹20 per person.

evidence.quote: Buddha Smriti Park How to Reach? Auto-rickshaws, city buses, taxis from Patna Junction. Timings 9 AM to 6 PM Entry Fees 20 Rs Per Person

BBS4.claim: Other relics come from monks of Thailand, Myanmar, Japan, South Korea and Sri Lanka; the meditation centre follows Nalanda monastery plans; there are a library, a museum with multimedia shows and a Park of Memories.

evidence.quote: brought by His Holiness the Dalai Lama and several monks from Thailand, Myanmar, Japan, South Korea and Sri Lanka
The meditation centre is based on the plans of the Nalanda University monasteries. It has 60 cells and one can view the beautiful stupa from each of them.
a library with numerous books on Buddhism, a museum as well as a Park of Memories
there are audio-visual and multimedia presentations about the life and teachings of Buddha in the museum

BVA1.claim: Vaishali was the capital of the Vajjika League, considered one of the first republics (c. 6th century BCE); the Buddha preached his last sermon here and Mahavira was born in a suburb, Kundagrama.

evidence.quote: It was the capital city of the Vajjika League considered one of the first examples of a republic that dates from c. 6th century BCE. Gautama Buddha preached his last sermon before his mahaparinirvana in c.
Gautama Buddha preached his last sermon before his mahaparinirvana
was born in Kundagrama which has been identified as a suburb of the city of Vaishali

BVA2.claim: At Kolhua, about 65 km north-west of Patna, Ashoka's lion pillar, a single piece of polished red sandstone 18.3 m high, stands beside a brick stupa and the Ramkund tank, commemorating the Buddha's last sermon.

evidence.quote: Kolhua is a famous Buddhist excavation site situated approximately 65 km North-West of Patna. The excavations have revealed the famous Ashokan Pillar having a statue of lion on the top.
It is made of a highly polished single piece of red sandstone, surmounted by a bell shaped capital, 18.3 m high. A life-size figure of a lion is placed on top of the pillar.
There is a small tank here known as Ramkund. This pillar beside a brick stupa at Kolhua commemorates Buddha's last sermon.

This pillar beside a brick stupa at Kolhua commemorates Buddha's last sermon. Vaishali THU 22 °C FRI 22 °C SAT 22 °C SUN 22 °C Photo Gallery At a Glance One of Emperor Ashoka’s edicts, this pillar stands as a testament to the spread of Buddhism in India.

BVA3.claim: The Second Buddhist Council met here in 383 BCE; the relic stupa and Ashokan pillar have been on UNESCO's tentative list since 2010.

evidence.quote: In 383 BCE the Second Buddhist council was convened here by King Kalashoka. It also contains one of the best-preserved of the Pillars of Ashoka from the 3rd century BCE, topped by a single Asiatic lion.
Since 2010, parts of the Vaishali archaeological site including the relic stupa and Asokan pillar have been considered a tentative site under the UNESCO World Heritage Sites list

BVA4.claim: Best September to April; reach by taxi or local bus from Hajipur; don't touch the pillar.

evidence.quote: Best Time to Visit : September to April.
Private taxis and local buses from Hajipur.
do not touch the pillar

BVA5.claim: The site is spread over a group of modern villages; a life-size lion tops the pillar.

evidence.quote: As an archaeological site it is spread over a group of modern villages
A life-size figure of a lion is placed on top of the pillar. There is a small tank here known as Ramkund.

BVK1.claim: The ruins of Vikramshila University are at Antichak in Kahalgaon, 38 km from Bhagalpur; founded by King Dharmapala, it was a famous centre of learning under the Palas.

evidence.quote: Situated at Antichak in Kahalgaon sub-division, 38 KM from Bhagalpur, ancient Vikramshila University was famous as a Centre of learning during the Pala dynasty. The university was established by the King Dharmapala.

The university was established by the King Dharmapala. Two things impressed Dharmapala and motivated him to establish the university; first, the rocky hillock anchored around the confluence of the Kosi and Ganga rivers at Bateshwar Sthan was not only a scenic attraction but also a popular Tantric site.

BVK2.claim: The ruins include stupas, monastery remains and meditation halls; best September to April; electronic gadgets need ASI permission.

evidence.quote: The ruins showcase intricate stupas, monastery remains, and meditation halls
Best Time to Visit : September to April.
Electronic Gadgets : Permission Required by ASI.

BVK3.claim: Dharmapala chose the site for its rocky hillock near the Kosi–Ganga confluence at Bateshwar Sthan and because the Ganga flows north here; reach it by bus or car from Bhagalpur.

evidence.quote: the rocky hillock anchored around the confluence of the Kosi and Ganga rivers at Bateshwar Sthan
the Ganga here was Uttar Vahini (flowing northwards)
Buses, private vehicles from Bhagalpur.

BVK4.claim: On the banks of the Ganga, the site offers a glimpse into ancient educational practices.

evidence.quote: Located on the banks of the Ganges
offering a glimpse into ancient educational practices

BBC1.claim: The Barabar Hill Caves near Makhdumpur in Jehanabad district, 24 km north of Gaya, are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, from the Maurya Empire, some with Ashokan inscriptions.

evidence.quote: he Barabar Hill Caves are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating from the Maurya Empire (322–185 BCE), some with Ashokan inscriptions, located in the Makhdumpur region of Jehanabad district, Bihar, India, 24 km (15 mi) north of Gaya.
24 km (15 mi) north of Gaya

BBC2.claim: Carved in granite with a highly polished 'Mauryan polish' interior and strong echoes, they were used by Ajivika ascetics; Barabar has four caves and nearby Nagarjuni three.

evidence.quote: carved entirely out of granite, with a highly polished internal surface

The caves were used by ascetics from the Ajivika sect, founded by Makkhali Gosala, a contemporary of Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, and of Mahavira, the last and 24th Tirthankara of Jainism.
These caves are situated in the twin hills of Barabar (four caves) and Nagarjuni (three caves)

BBC3.claim: The Lomas Rishi cave's carved entrance is the earliest surviving chaitya arch; the caves appear, as the 'Marabar' caves, in E. M. Forster's A Passage to India.

evidence.quote: The sculptured surround to the entrance to the Lomas Rishi Cave is the earliest survival of the ogee shaped "chaitya arch"
The caves were featured – located in a fictitious Marabar – in the book A Passage to India

BBC4.claim: Best September to April; reach by auto or taxi from Jehanabad, with some trekking.

evidence.quote: Best Time to Visit : September to April.
Auto-rickshaws and taxis from Jehanabad town, some trekking may be required

BBC5.claim: Inscriptions name 'King Piyadasi' (Ashoka) and 'Devanampiya Dasaratha', his grandson; the Lomas Rishi facade imitates timber architecture with a row of carved elephants.

evidence.quote: to correspond respectively to Ashoka (reigned 273–232 BCE) and his grandson, Dasharatha Maurya
Lomas Rishi Cave has an arch-like facade that imitates contemporary timber architecture.
carved elephants proceed in a row along the curved architrave

BRF1.claim: Rohtasgarh Fort sits on a plateau about 1,500 feet up, around two hours from Sasaram to the foot of the hill; about 2,000 limestone steps at Medha Ghat take an hour and a half to climb.

evidence.quote: Location and ascent It takes around two hours from the district headquarters at Sasaram to reach the foot of the hill over which is the Rohtas Fort. The fort is situated at about 1500 feet above sea level.
The fort is situated at about 1500 feet above sea level. There are about 2000 odd limestone steps at Medha Ghat meant for the most common mode of ascent to the fort on foot at present.
There are about 2000 odd limestone steps at Medha Ghat meant for the most common mode of ascent to the fort on foot at present.
For the visitor they are an exhausting climb of an hour and a half. At the end of the climb, one reaches the boundary wall of the fort.

BRF2.claim: Legend links the fort to Rohitaswa, son of King Harishchandra; the oldest record found on it is a 7th-century inscription of Sasanka, and Sher Shah Suri later strengthened it.

evidence.quote: the Fort is ascribed to have been constructed by the legendary Rohitaswa, son of the great King Harish Chandra
The oldest historical record found on the fort is an inscription which is ascribed to the 7th century
later strengthened by Sher Shah Suri

BRF3.claim: The complex has gates, palaces, temples and reservoirs; in the rains a waterfall pours over the fortifications. Best September to April; taxis and local guides from Sasaram.

evidence.quote: The fort complex includes gates, palaces, temples, and reservoirs
A lovely waterfall is seen during the rains, which falls over the fortifications
Best Time to Visit : September to April.
Private taxis and local guides from Sasaram.

BRF4.claim: Streams and fertile soil let the garrison hold out for months; thick forests surrounded the hill; it could only be taken by deceit; another mile's walk leads to the ruins.

evidence.quote: so that the inhabitants of the fort could hold out for months against any enemy besieging the fort
Thick forests and wild animals surrounded the hill
could not be taken by force but only by means of deceit
From here one has to walk another mile or so before the ruins of Rohtas can be seen.

BSG1.claim: Shergarh, or Badal Garh, is a hill fort on the eastern bank of the Durgawati about 32 km south-west of Sasaram, left unattended for more than 400 years.

evidence.quote: The Hill Fort of Sher-Garh also at times known as ‘Badal Garh’, has remained mysterious and has been now lying unattended for more than 400 years, on the eastern banks of the river Durgawati,
Situated about 32 kms south-west of the town of Sasaram

BSG2.claim: Its origin is a mystery: Buchanan assumed Sher Shah built it, but the 1966 Shahabad Gazetteer argues it was an older Rajput stronghold named after Sher Shah.

evidence.quote: The mysterious origin and history of Shergarh pose a lot of unanswered questions.
Francis Buchanan assumed without much basis that it may have been constructed by Sher Shah
the fort had existed from before and was the stronghold of the Rajput chieftains

BSG3.claim: The steep path climbs through gorges and jungle to ruins with views over the Durgawati valley; gateways, reservoirs and inscriptions remain. Best September to April; carry water; taxis and buses from Sasaram.

commands a magnificent view of the distant range of hills and the valley of Durgawati

Private taxis and local buses from Sasaram.

BSG4.claim: The fort separates Rohtas and Kaimur districts; its rock top has bastions and bulwarks; Buchanan visited in 1813 and compared it to Durham Castle.

evidence.quote: separating the districts of Rohtas and Kaimur in Bihar
well-fortified by a number of bastions and bulwarks

to the European castle of Durham

BMD1.claim: Mundeshwari Devi Temple on the Mundeshwari Hills in Kaimur, dedicated to Shiva and Shakti, is considered one of the oldest functional temples in the world, with worship unbroken; it has been ASI-protected since 1915.

evidence.quote: is considered as the ‘oldest Functional' temple of the world as rituals have been performed here without a break
Maa Mundeshwari Devi Temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and Shakti and is positioned in the Mundeshwari Hills. The temple also has deities of Ganesha, Surya and Vishnu.
has been a protected monument since 1915

BMD2.claim: It is the oldest specimen of the Nagara style; a four-faced Shiva linga stands at the centre and Durga as Mundeshwari in a niche; Ramnavami and Shivratri draw pilgrims.

evidence.quote: Mundeshwari Temple is the oldest specimen of the Nagara style of temple architecture. Around the seventh century AD, Shaivism became the prevalent religion and Viniteswara, which was a minor deity, emerged as the presiding deity of the temple.
The Chatur Mukhalingam (Lingam with four faces)
So, the image of Durga was installed in a niche along one wall of the temple
The festivals of Ramnavami and Shivrartri hold special charm

evidence.quote: Best Time to Visit: September to April

evidence.quote: The temple also has deities of Ganesha, Surya and Vishnu. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) dates the temple to 108 AD and has been a protected monument since 1915.
This octagonal temple

BJM1.claim: The Jal Mandir at Pawapuri marks where Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, attained moksha and was cremated; the white marble temple stands in a lotus-filled tank.

evidence.quote: The Jal Mandir (literally water temple) marks the spot where Lord Mahavira was cremated. It is said that there was such a huge demand for ashes from his funeral pyre that Jal mandir as the name suggests is a temple in the middle of a lake blooming with lotuses.

The temple holds immense significance as it marks the spot where Mahavira attained moksha (liberation) and was cremated.
It is uniquely situated in the middle of a serene lotus-filled tank
The temple’s white marble architecture

evidence.quote: Best Time To Visit : September to April.

evidence.quote: It is said that there was such a huge demand for ashes from his funeral pyre
Pilgrims from across the country visit Jal Mandir

BGK1.claim: Gridhakuta (Vulture Peak) near Rajgir is where the Buddha is said to have preached the Lotus Sermon; it was one of his favourite places to meditate, and the rock looks like a vulture's head.

evidence.quote: This is one of the most ancient sites where the Buddha is said to have preached his Lotus Sermon. Quite true to the meaning of its name as Vulture Peak indeed the peak appears as the shape of a vulture's head with a natural stone formation.
Quite true to the meaning of its name as Vulture Peak indeed the peak appears as the shape of a vulture's head
was amongst the favorite meditating place of the Buddha

BGK2.claim: Reach it by ropeway or on foot from Rajgir; open 6 am to 7 pm, free.

BGK3.claim: Best September to April; keep silent and respect Buddhist traditions.

evidence.quote: Best Time to Visit : September to April.
Maintain silence, respect Buddhist traditions

BGK4.claim: One of the most significant Buddhist sites; called Gujjhakut in Buddhist texts; the peak has no man-made grandeur; a Buddha statue found here is in the Nalanda museum; paths lead toward Ghora Katora lake.

evidence.quote: Gridhakut Hill (Vulture’s Peak) is one of the most significant Buddhist sites
The place is also referred as “Gujjhakut” in Buddhist text.
A statue of the Buddha (600 BCE) was found here and currently housed at Archeological Museum of Nalanda.
the path leading to Ghoda Katora Lake

BSS1.claim: The Tomb of Sher Shah Suri in Sasaram, built for the founder of the Sur Empire, was completed on 16 August 1545, about three months after his death.

evidence.quote: he Tomb of Sher Shah Suri is a mausoleum located in Sasaram, in the Indian state of Bihar. Sher Shah Suri, who was the founder of the Sur Empire, commissioned the tomb for himself.
It was completed on 16 August 1545, about three months after his death. It is situated on a square plinth in the middle of an artificial lake, accessible by a causeway.

BSS2.claim: It stands on a square plinth in an artificial lake reached by a causeway: a three-storeyed octagonal sandstone building under a large dome, once painted and tiled, with chhatris on the upper storeys.

evidence.quote: It is situated on a square plinth in the middle of an artificial lake, accessible by a causeway. The tomb, made out of sandstone, was originally painted in bright colours and decorated with glazed tiles.
The tomb, made out of sandstone, was originally painted in bright colours and decorated with glazed tiles. It is a three-storied octagonal building, surmounted by a large dome.
It is a three-storied octagonal building, surmounted by a large dome. Chhatris are located on each edge of the second and third stories.

BSS3.claim: The largest mausoleum in India when completed, it is a key example of Indo-Islamic architecture and a monument of national importance; Sher Shah died on 22 May 1545 in a gunpowder explosion at Kalinjar.

evidence.quote: The tomb, which was the largest mausoleum in India at the time of its completion, is considered a significant example of Indo-Islamic architecture and one of the most important monuments in Bihar.
It is listed as a monument of national importance. == History == The tomb was commissioned by Sher Shah during his lifetime, possibly in 1542.
Sher Shah died on 22 May 1545 in an accidental gunpowder explosion outside Kalinjar Fort

BSS4.claim: Chhatris stand on the edges of the second and third storeys and a veranda with three arched openings on each side runs around the tomb; it is a key example of Indo-Islamic architecture.

evidence.quote: Chhatris are located on each edge of the second and third stories. A veranda runs along the circumference of the tomb, with each side having three arched openings.

places.name: Gaya
places.summary: Bihar's second city on the Phalgu, home of the Vishnupad Temple and gateway to Bodh Gaya.
places.seoTitle: Gaya: Vishnupad Temple, Pind Daan, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Gaya on the Phalgu River, 100 km south of Patna: the Vishnupad Temple, pind daan rituals, nearby Bodh Gaya, and how to get there.

overview.text: Gaya is Bihar's second-largest city, 100 km south of Patna on the banks of the Phalgu River, which the Ramayana calls the Niranjana. Rocky hills, among them Mangla-Gauri, Ram-Shila and Brahmayoni, enclose it on three sides, with the river on the fourth. The city is said to take its name from the mythological demon Gayasur, and it is holy to Hindus, Buddhists and Jains alike. For Hindus, Gaya is above all the place for pind daan, the rite for the salvation of ancestors performed at the Vishnupad Temple on the riverbank; the Ramayana tells how Rama came here to perform it for his father Dasharatha. Gaya is also linked to the Buddha's enlightenment, at nearby Bodh Gaya. Gaya International Airport serves both, and the train from Patna takes about two hours.

places.summary: Gaya's riverside temple of Vishnu's footprint, centre of the pind daan rites.
places.seoTitle: Vishnupad Temple, Gaya: Pind Daan, Timings, Rules
places.seoDescription: Vishnupad Temple, Gaya: built in 1787 by Ahilyabai, enshrining Vishnu's footprint; the centre of pind daan. Phones and cameras prohibited.

overview.text: The Vishnupad Temple stands on the bank of the Phalgu River in Gaya and is dedicated to Vishnu. Its sanctum enshrines a footprint of the god, the Vishnupad, imprinted in rock, and the temple is one of the most important places in India for pind daan, the offering made for the salvation of ancestors. Tradition holds that Rama himself came to Gaya to perform pind daan for his father Dasharatha, as the Ramayana relates. The present temple was built in 1787 by Queen Ahilyabai. Dress modestly, take off your shoes, and note that mobile phones, cameras and other electronic gadgets are not allowed inside.

places.name: Great Buddha Statue (80 Feet Buddha)
places.summary: Bodh Gaya's 80-foot seated Buddha, consecrated by the Dalai Lama in 1989.
places.seoTitle: Great Buddha Statue, Bodh Gaya: The 80-Foot Buddha
places.seoDescription: The 80-foot Great Buddha in Bodh Gaya: sandstone and red granite, consecrated by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1989; 2 km from the Mahabodhi Temple.

overview.text: The Great Buddha Statue, usually called the 80 Feet Buddha, is one of the landmarks of Bodh Gaya and one of the tallest Buddha statues in India. Built of sandstone blocks and red granite, it shows the Buddha seated in deep meditation, and around it stand smaller statues of his disciples. The foundation stone was laid in 1982, and the statue was consecrated by the 14th Dalai Lama on 18 November 1989. It stands about 2 km from the Mahabodhi Temple and is one of the regular stops for pilgrims and tourists making the circuit of Bodh Gaya's monasteries and temples. The site is easy to reach by auto-rickshaw, e-rickshaw or taxi, and Gaya International Airport is about 7 km away. Dress modestly and keep silent around the statue.

places.name: Buddha Smriti Park
places.summary: A 22-acre memorial park by Patna Junction with the 200-ft Karuna Stupa.
places.seoTitle: Buddha Smriti Park, Patna: Karuna Stupa, Timings, Entry Fee
places.seoDescription: Buddha Smriti Park near Patna Junction: the 200-ft Pataliputra Karuna Stupa with a Vaishali relic, Bodhi trees, museum; open 9–6, ₹20 entry.

overview.text: Buddha Smriti Park is a 22-acre park on Fraser Road, close to Patna Junction and opposite the Mahavir Mandir, created by the Government of Bihar to mark the 2554th birth anniversary of the Buddha. Two Bodhi trees planted by the Dalai Lama flank a statue of the Buddha at its centre. The most prominent feature is the 200-foot Pataliputra Karuna Stupa, a circular building that houses, in a glass enclosure, a relic of the Buddha said to be one of the eight original relics excavated from Vaishali, along with other relics given by monks from Thailand, Myanmar, Japan, South Korea and Sri Lanka. The park also has a meditation centre modelled on the monasteries of Nalanda, with 60 cells that each look onto the stupa, a library of books on Buddhism, a museum with multimedia shows on the Buddha's life, and a Park of Memories.

places.name: Vaishali
places.summary: Ancient republic and Buddhist site north of Patna, with Ashoka's lion pillar at Kolhua.
places.seoTitle: Vaishali: Ashoka Pillar at Kolhua, Relic Stupa, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Vaishali, 65 km from Patna: capital of an ancient republic, Ashoka's lion pillar and stupa at Kolhua, the Buddha's last sermon; best September–April.

overview.text: Vaishali, north of Patna, was the capital of the Vajjika League, considered one of the first examples of a republic, around the 6th century BCE. It is a place of pilgrimage for Buddhists and Jains: the Buddha preached his last sermon here before his final passing, and Mahavira was born at Kundagrama, identified as a suburb of the ancient city. The Second Buddhist Council met here in 383 BCE. Today Vaishali is an archaeological landscape spread across several villages. Its highlight is at Kolhua, about 65 km north-west of Patna, where Ashoka's pillar, a single shaft of polished red sandstone 18.3 metres high topped by a life-size lion, stands beside a brick stupa and a small tank called Ramkund, marking the Buddha's last sermon. Since 2010 the relic stupa and pillar have been on UNESCO's tentative list.

places.name: Vikramshila University Ruins
places.summary: The excavated Pala-era Buddhist university near Bhagalpur.
places.seoDescription: Ruins of Vikramshila at Antichak, 38 km from Bhagalpur: King Dharmapala's Buddhist university of the Pala era, with its great stupa and monasteries.

overview.text: The ruins of Vikramshila lie at Antichak in Kahalgaon, 38 km from Bhagalpur, on the banks of the Ganga. Vikramshila was one of the great Buddhist universities of ancient India, founded by King Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty and famous as a centre of learning under the Palas. Bihar Tourism explains why he chose the spot: a rocky hillock near the confluence of the Kosi and the Ganga at Bateshwar Sthan was both scenic and a popular Tantric site, and the Ganga here flows north (Uttar Vahini), which made it a place of pilgrimage. The excavated site shows the remains of stupas, monasteries and meditation halls, a glimpse of how monks studied and lived. It is best visited between September and April, and photography with gadgets needs permission from the Archaeological Survey of India.

places.name: Barabar Caves
places.summary: India's oldest surviving rock-cut caves, polished by Mauryan craftsmen in the 3rd century BCE.
places.seoTitle: Barabar Caves: Mauryan Rock-Cut Caves near Gaya
places.seoDescription: Barabar Caves near Gaya: India's oldest surviving rock-cut caves, Mauryan-polished granite chambers with Ashokan inscriptions and the Lomas Rishi arch.

overview.text: The Barabar Hill Caves, near Makhdumpur in Jehanabad district about 24 km north of Gaya, are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India. They date from the Maurya Empire in the 3rd century BCE, and some bear dedications from Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha. Four caves are cut into the granite of Barabar Hill and three more into neighbouring Nagarjuni Hill. Their inner chambers were carved entirely out of hard granite and polished to a mirror-like finish, the famous Mauryan polish, and they produce remarkable echoes. The caves were made for ascetics of the Ajivika sect. The entrance of the Lomas Rishi cave, carved to imitate a wooden hut with elephants along its arch, is the earliest surviving example of the chaitya arch. E. M. Forster used the caves, as the 'Marabar' caves, in A Passage to India.

places.name: Rohtasgarh Fort
places.summary: A vast plateau fort above the Sone, reached by 2,000 steps from Medha Ghat.
places.seoTitle: Rohtasgarh Fort: Trek, History, Getting There from Sasaram
places.seoDescription: Rohtasgarh Fort, Rohtas district: a plateau fort 1,500 ft up, reached by about 2,000 limestone steps; gates, palaces and reservoirs; best September–April.

overview.text: Rohtasgarh Fort covers a plateau on top of a hill in Rohtas district, about two hours' drive from Sasaram to the foot of the hill. Its sides rise steeply, and streams and fertile soil on top once let the garrison hold out for months against a siege; thick forest added a natural barrier, and the fort was said to be taken only by deceit. Visitors still climb on foot, up about 2,000 limestone steps at Medha Ghat, an exhausting hour and a half, to reach the walls at around 1,500 feet, then walk another mile or so to the ruins. In the monsoon a waterfall spills over the fortifications. Legend ties the fort to Rohitaswa, son of King Harishchandra; the oldest inscription found here is from the 7th century, and Sher Shah Suri later strengthened it. Gates, palaces, temples and reservoirs survive across the plateau.

places.summary: A ruined hill fort above the Durgawati gorge, of uncertain origin.
places.seoTitle: Shergarh Fort near Sasaram: Hill Fort above the Durgawati
places.seoDescription: Shergarh (Badal Garh) Fort, 32 km south-west of Sasaram: a ruined hill fort above the Durgawati valley, reached by a steep jungle path.

overview.text: Shergarh Fort, also called Badal Garh, crowns a rocky hill on the eastern bank of the Durgawati River about 32 km south-west of Sasaram, on the border of Rohtas and Kaimur districts. Unattended for more than 400 years, it is a natural hill fort whose summit is ringed by bastions and bulwarks. The approach is a steep, winding path through gorges and jungle, and the ruined top commands a magnificent view over distant hills and the Durgawati valley; the surveyor Francis Buchanan, who came in 1813, compared it to the castle at Durham. Who built it is uncertain. Buchanan assumed it was Sher Shah Suri, but the Shahabad Gazetteer of 1966 argues the fort was an older Rajput stronghold that took its name from Sher Shah. Gateways, water reservoirs and old inscriptions survive. Carry water and come prepared for a climb.

places.name: Mundeshwari Devi Temple
places.summary: An ancient octagonal hilltop temple in Kaimur, worshipped without a break.
places.seoTitle: Mundeshwari Devi Temple, Kaimur: Ancient Hill Temple
places.seoDescription: Mundeshwari Devi Temple in Kaimur: an ancient octagonal Nagara-style shrine to Shiva and Shakti, considered one of the oldest functioning temples.

overview.text: Mundeshwari Devi Temple stands on the Mundeshwari Hills in Kaimur district and is dedicated to Shiva and Shakti, with images of Ganesha, Surya and Vishnu as well. Because worship is believed to have continued here without a break since ancient times, it is considered one of the oldest functioning temples in the world. The Archaeological Survey of India has protected it since 1915, and it is the oldest surviving example of the Nagara style of temple building, with an unusual octagonal plan. Over the centuries the presiding deity changed: a four-faced Shiva linga, the Chatur Mukhalingam, still holds the central place, while the goddess Mundeshwari, a form of Durga, was installed in a niche in one wall when the Chero rulers of the Kaimur hills, worshippers of Shakti, came to power. Ramnavami and Shivratri bring large crowds.

places.name: Jal Mandir, Pawapuri
places.summary: The white marble Jain water temple where Mahavira was cremated.
places.seoTitle: Jal Mandir, Pawapuri: Where Mahavira Attained Moksha
places.seoDescription: Jal Mandir at Pawapuri, near Rajgir and Nalanda: the white marble Jain temple in a lotus tank marking where Mahavira was cremated.

overview.text: The Jal Mandir, or water temple, at Pawapuri in Nalanda district is one of the holiest places in Jainism. It marks the spot where Mahavira, the 24th and last Tirthankara, attained moksha and was cremated. Tradition speaks of a huge demand for the ashes from his funeral pyre, and the temple now stands in the middle of a lotus-filled tank. Built of white marble, it is said to have been raised by Mahavira's elder brother, King Nandivardhan, and its main object of worship is an ancient charan paduka, a carved pair of Mahavira's footprints. Pilgrims from across the country come to pay homage, and the calm water and white temple make it a beautiful sight. Pawapuri is easily reached by auto or taxi from Nalanda or Rajgir.

places.seoTitle: Gridhakuta (Vulture Peak), Rajgir: Where the Buddha Preached
places.seoDescription: Gridhakuta, the Vulture Peak at Rajgir: where the Buddha preached the Lotus Sermon; reach by ropeway or trek; open 6 am–7 pm, free.

overview.text: Gridhakuta, the Vulture Peak, is a rocky hilltop above Rajgir that is one of the most significant Buddhist sites in India. The Buddha is said to have preached the Lotus Sermon here, and it was one of his favourite places for meditation; Buddhist texts call it Gujjhakut. True to its name, a natural rock formation on the peak looks like a vulture's head. The summit is devoid of any man-made grandeur, yet visitors still feel a deep sense of spiritual power here. A statue of the Buddha found on the hill is now in the Archaeological Museum at Nalanda. The views over the forested hills and the path towards Ghora Katora lake add to the walk. Climb on foot or take the ropeway from Rajgir; the site is open from 6 am to 7 pm and is free.

overview.text: Kundalpur is a village just 1.6 km from the ruins of Nalanda, and the Digambar sect of Jains believes that Mahavira, the 24th and last Tirthankara, was born here. The village has many Jain temples, and its location close to Nalanda and the ancient city of Rajgir makes it a popular stop for both pilgrims and other travellers on the circuit. The present temple is a recent building. In a separate building, images of 72 Jinas are set out for offerings, and the temple offers good accommodation for devotees who want to stay. Visitors should dress modestly and keep quiet during prayers. Kundalpur is easy to reach by auto-rickshaw or taxi from Nalanda town, right next to the Nalanda ruins.

places.seoTitle: Sher Shah Suri Tomb, Sasaram: Tomb in the Lake
places.seoDescription: Sher Shah Suri's tomb in Sasaram: a 1545 octagonal sandstone mausoleum in an artificial lake, once India's largest, reached by a causeway.

overview.text: The Tomb of Sher Shah Suri rises from the middle of an artificial lake in Sasaram, Bihar. Sher Shah, the founder of the Sur Empire, commissioned it for himself, but he died on 22 May 1545 in an accidental gunpowder explosion while besieging Kalinjar Fort, and the tomb was completed about three months later, on 16 August 1545. Built of sandstone on a square plinth reached by a causeway, it is a three-storeyed octagonal building crowned by a great dome, with chhatris on the edges of the upper storeys and a veranda of arched openings all round. It was originally painted in bright colours and decorated with glazed tiles. When finished it was the largest mausoleum in India, and it is regarded as a landmark of Indo-Islamic architecture and a monument of national importance.
